The check has been dormant for every store since it was written, so the store's own arithmetic proof sits in the capture and the flag cannot see it.

MEASURED over the 62 open outlier flags in out\guards-2026-09-02.json (plus 7 wow flags = 69 entries; the alert's '83 other' also counts MULTIBUY/BASIS/PACKBASIS keys): the cheapest row carries a store-published unit price in the union captures for 38 of them; 33 agree with ours within max(half a cent, 3%) (oats included: ours 0.0499 vs $0.05/oz), 0 disagree, 5 are unit-family mismatches where the store prices per each/oz and the board prices per oz/each (Hummus $0.35/ea, Pomegranate $0.80/oz, Keto Buns 34.1 c/oz, Popsicles 4.1 c/oz, Insect Spray 7.4 c/fl oz) and 24 have no store unit price (Aldi, Baker's, Fareway, Family Fare, Hy-Vee cheapest rows). Board-wide: 906 Sam's + Walmart cells, 687 verifiable and agreeing, 0 disagreeing, 168 unit-family mismatches, 51 without a unit price. The one board-wide near-miss is exactly the rounding boundary: Sam's saltines ours 0.155 vs '$0.15/oz' (0.005 apart), so the tolerance must be half a cent INCLUSIVE with float slack.

Out of scope, stated once: the 83 pre-existing open flags are not worked here. The arithmetic verification above says only that the store's own per-unit reproduces ours; it does not judge product identity (e.g. the Walmart 'Ham (deli / sliced)' cheapest is a 7 lb ham at $1.98/lb, arithmetically verified and possibly the wrong product), which stays with the food-category / known-wrong / name-drift guards.

the two numbers the alert printed are the SAME FILE measured in two units: 2959184 is the character count of the UTF-8-decoded board, 2961318 is its byte count. The board carries 2134 multi-byte characters, and 2961318 - 2959184 = 2134 exactly.

capture-run.ps1:942 reads the committed side as `(& git -C $repo show HEAD:public/board.json | Out-String)`. surface_fix.what: read the committed blob byte-safely at the board.json read-after-write and compare bytes to bytes
surface_fix.exact_change: capture-run.ps1:942-948: replace the `git show | Out-String` text read and the string `-ne` with a byte comparison: obtain the blob as bytes (never through a PowerShell string), hash it with SHA256, hash the live response's raw bytes (Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing .RawContentStream or .Content as [byte[]]), and report stale only when the two hashes differ; the stale message names both hashes and both byte counts.

items.root_cause: a committed blob is read for byte-comparison through PowerShell's native-command TEXT pipeline (`git show | Out-String`), which decodes with the console code page. The comparison is therefore between two different decodings of identical bytes. The same pattern sits at capture-run.ps1:915 for smp-feed and survives only by accident, because that path ConvertFrom-Json's the blob and compares one ASCII field (`generated`) rather than the whole string - so the defect is latent there and fires the moment anyone compares more.

root_fix.what: one byte-safe way to read a committed blob, used by BOTH call sites, that never round-trips the payload through a decoded string: write the blob to a file and compare SHA256 against the hash of the live response bytes
root_fix.exact_change: add lib\git-blob-lib.ps1 with Get-CommittedBlobBytes -Repo <path> -Spec 'HEAD:public/board.json' (runs `git cat-file blob <spec>` with stdout captured as a byte stream via System.Diagnostics.Process into a scratch file or MemoryStream, returns [byte[]] or $null on a non-zero exit; no stderr redirect under EAP=Stop) and Get-Sha256Hex([byte[]]); capture-run.ps1:915 (smp-feed) and :942 (board.json) both call it; smp-feed keeps its `generated` comparison for the poll loop (decode the bytes as UTF-8 explicitly with [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString before ConvertFrom-Json) and adds the same hash comparison after the poll succeeds; board.json compares hashes only.
